purpose: Machine-readable companion to spec.md. spec.md is normative for prose semantics; this file is normative for limits, check order, error registry, identity scopes and numeric tolerances so that implementations and tests share one source.

canonicalization.digest: SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the canonical serialization
semantic_projection: nodes sorted ascending by node id
each adjacency neighbour array sorted ascending by node id
all remaining member order is positional (nodes index, position component)
JSON object member order is irrelevant because JCS sorts members
canonicalization.id_order_rule: node and image ids are restricted to ASCII by limits.id.pattern, so ascending byte order, code point order and UTF-16 code unit order coincide

revision.note: 9007199254740991 is 2^53-1, the largest integer exactly representable in binary64. Gaps are allowed; out-of-order legal revisions are accepted.

coordinate.note: Validity bound only; it is not a tolerance. Source coordinates are preserved exactly once accepted.

coincidence.compare: level set: distance exactly equal to the threshold is rejected

normative_rule.arithmetic: IEEE 754 binary64, round to nearest, ties to even
normative_rule.evaluation: dx=fl(px-qx), dy=fl(py-qy), dz=fl(pz-qz); s=fl(fl(fl(dx*dx)+fl(dy*dy))+fl(dz*dz)); reject iff s <= limit_squared
normative_rule.candidate_window: W=fl(tau*fl(1+8u)); the sweep only visits pairs with |fl(px-qx)| <= W and then applies the same final comparison
normative_rule.window_proof: if s <= limit_squared then each rounded square is at most s (the sum of non-negative rounded terms cannot be smaller than any single rounded term), so dx^2 <= s/(1-u) <= tau^2(1+8u)/(1-u); therefore |dx| <= tau*sqrt((1+8u)/(1-u)) < tau(1+8u) = W for the frozen constants, so the candidate window cannot miss a rejectable pair
normative_rule.reason: sqrt(dx^2+dy^2+dz^2) of an exact 1e-6 separation can round slightly above the stored threshold double; the directed squared-distance rule makes the inclusive boundary deterministic and language independent

coincidence.why_slack: without the directed slack the inclusive boundary would be untestable and language dependent; the 8u relative slack (8.881784197001252e-16 = 8 * 2^-53) is far below any user-visible distance
coincidence.compatibility_note: the candidate window was previously +/- tau, which missed the axial nextafter(1e-6,+inf) pair while the diagonal pair was rejected; gtp.3 uses W and rejects both (declared behaviour change R-06)

import_id.note: R-09d: the receipt schema already constrained import_id; gtp.3 writes the same charset and length into the normative rules and spec 7.4 and adds output boundary examples

json.duplicate_object_keys: rejected before the value is inserted into the object
json.number_literals: RFC 8259 grammar, then must be representable as finite binary64 without non-zero underflow to zero

versions.wire: ptg-graph/1.0 (exact match, no negotiation in v1)

frame_rule.redeclaration: any change to coordinate_system while reusing graph_id is FRAME_CONFLICT
frame_rule.new_frame: assign a new graph_id and record the conversion provenance in the producer
frame_rule.hook: checked inside the same transaction as key binding and snapshot insert

pre_validation_failure.detail: transport/syntax/version/headers/structure/graph/geometry/topology failure happens before the identity stage; no binding or record exists, so the same key may be reused for a corrected request

identity_conflict.detail: 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT/FRAME_CONFLICT/REVISION_CONFLICT does not create a new binding; the existing mapping and snapshot stay untouched

transaction_rollback.detail: a failed transaction rolls back snapshot, key mapping, revision binding and frame registration together; a retry with the same key and bytes may create the import

storage_failure_or_busy.state: unbound unless the commit actually completed
storage_failure_or_busy.detail: 500 STORAGE_FAILURE and 503 IMPORT_BUSY send no success receipt; the client retries with the original key and the byte-identical snapshot, and a 200 on retry means the earlier attempt had committed

committed_but_receipt_lost.detail: the commit succeeded; a retry with the same key and the same bytes returns 200 with the same import_id, while the same key with different bytes returns 409

idempotency_key_lifecycle.real_transaction: NOT_RUN; P5-I owns the database transaction

responsibility.rule: PTG must fully transform camera, screen/viewport, reference-plane and object-local coordinates into the fixed graph frame before submitting; the wire carries only the resulting XYZ positions, the coordinate_system declaration and the source declaration
responsibility.display_state: camera, viewport, work plane and reference image plane are editor display state only; they must not be sent on the wire and are not part of source_graph, identity or semantic_digest
responsibility.no_projection: three-dimensional information must not be flattened into a 2D representation before submission; a screen-space point is not a valid control point
responsibility.edit_rule: switching the view does not change the source graph; creating or editing a node is a graph edit and must write the actual spatial position into a new revision
responsibility.reference_plane: a reference image plane only provides source provenance (source.reference_image_ids); it does not carry geometry and cannot replace XYZ coordinates

acceptance_scenarios.check: camera/work_plane members are FIELD_UNKNOWN; source_graph has no display state
switching camera/viewport/work plane keeps source_graph values, identity and semantic_digest
an edit after a view switch creates a new revision with the real 3D position (non-zero Z preserved)
a blank scene cannot invent control points
a reference image plane maps to source provenance only
a non-unit object transform is applied before submission
a ray without a unique intersection must not guess coordinates

view_transform.real_ui: NOT_RUN; PTG-1/PTG-2 execute the real UI scenarios and return fixed-version evidence

browser_matrix.acceptance_entry: PTG-1/PTG-4 browser matrix with fixed versions, address and logs/screenshots returned to GTP

three_point_internal_start.acceptance_entry: internal-start counterexample uses a 3-point chain; GTP fixes invalid-internal-start and PTG corrects the wording

stages.name: headers
checks: Idempotency-Key presence, length, character set, single header value

stages.name: graph
checks: adjacency key set equals node id set

stages.name: geometry
checks: no pair of control points at or below the coincidence threshold

stages.name: topology
checks: exactly two degree-1 endpoints (open chain, no cycle)
n_terminal_node is one of the endpoints

stages.name: identity
checks: atomic snapshot plus key binding commit
stages.p0_status: reference model only; real transaction in P5-I

semantic_checks.name: adjacency_key_set
semantic_checks.detail: unexpected keys first (sorted), then missing node ids (sorted)

semantic_checks.name: neighbour_reference_exists
semantic_checks.selection: smallest (referencing node id, unknown neighbour id) pair, independent of the neighbour array order; duplicate occurrences of the selected unknown neighbour use its first index in the original array (R-02)
semantic_checks.located_by: node_ids = [unknown id, referencing node id] sorted
semantic_checks.equivalence: reordered neighbour arrays select the same semantic object and report the same code and node_ids; the field index follows the bytes because it is an input location, not part of the error identity

semantic_checks.name: no_coincident_control_points
semantic_checks.located_by: node_ids = [id a, id b] sorted by id order of the visited pair

first_error_scope.structure: field_order, then error code priority, then field text (rules.field_rank / rules.error_sort_key)
first_error_scope.graph_geometry_topology: semantic_checks order; inside one check the check's own stable semantic-object selection decides which error is first. field_order does not apply to these stages (R-07)
first_error_scope.field_identity: for graph/geometry/topology the reported field is the location in the original input; the semantic identity of an error is (code, node_ids, selected semantic object). Array reordering can move field while code/node_ids stay stable (R-02)
first_error_scope.pair_order: reported node_ids are sorted ascending and de-duplicated

error_stage_policy.reported_stage: the stage that actually failed in this validation run (R-10)
error_stage_policy.registry_stage: the allowed stage set for the code; JSON_SYNTAX is shared by transport (UTF-8/BOM) and syntax (RFC 8259) and is therefore registered as transport|syntax
error_stage_policy.wire_projection: the wire error document never contains stage; the tool report keeps it for diagnostics only
shared_code_examples: invalid-bom / invalid-utf8 -> JSON_SYNTAX with reported stage transport
invalid-nan / invalid-json-trailing-comma -> JSON_SYNTAX with reported stage syntax

full.headers: Idempotency-Key is mandatory; absence is IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID at the headers stage
full.identity_stage: service-only hand-off; the CLI reports it SKIPPED
full.service_status: http_status 201 (candidate; 200 for an existing equivalent import)
full.callers: public CLI default; tools.validation.validate_import default; future P5-I HTTP entry

graph.headers: request headers are outside scope; an absent key makes the headers stage SKIPPED
graph.service_status: no service status claimed; http_status is null
graph.callers: library/test callers that validate graph content only; must select this mode explicitly (CLI --mode graph)

validation_modes.migration: the legacy require_idempotency_key flag is kept as an alias (True -> full, False -> graph); gtp.3 makes the default full for the public CLI and the application entry so a complete request cannot silently skip the mandatory header

an object member name occurs twice
number literal overflows binary64 or underflows non-zero to zero
JSON nesting depth exceeds the contract limit
Content-Encoding is not identity
Content-Type is not application/json with an optional utf-8 charset

error_registry.note: reserved: P0 does not require a local single-user server to enforce rate limits, but the client rule is frozen

error_registry.summary: derived similarity transform cannot round-trip local geometry within the frozen tolerance; the source graph is preserved
error_registry.note: derivation-stage code, not part of the PTG import error registry

error_registry.summary: the requested derived transform is not a proper similarity transform (reflection, non-uniform or non-positive scale)
error_registry.note: derivation-stage code, not part of the PTG import error registry

source_graph.rule: accepted and re-read source coordinates compare exactly component by component as binary64 values (IEEE 754 value equality, where -0 equals 0); a change of any single component is a content change
source_graph.why: content identity must not depend on a tolerance; otherwise a small but real edit inside a large coordinate frame can be mistaken for a repeat submission

derived_transform.formula_forward: bound_fwd(p) = gamma * (abs(s) * sqrt(3) * (A(p) + A(c)) + A(t)) + abs(s) * eps_R * (A(p) + A(c))
derived_transform.formula_inverse: bound_inv(m) = gamma * (sqrt(3) * (A(m) + A(t)) / abs(s) + A(c)) + eps_R * (A(m) + A(t)) / abs(s)
derived_transform.notation: A(x) = max(abs(x1),abs(x2),abs(x3)); gamma = 10*u/(1-10*u); eps_R = max abs component of (R^T R - I), the orthogonality residual of the stored rotation; sqrt(3) bounds the infinity norm of a proper rotation row

rotation_residual.definition: eps_R = max abs component of (R^T R - I); eps_det = abs(det(R) - 1)
rotation_residual.residual_max_rule: eps_R <= 64*u and eps_det <= 64*u, where u = 2^-53; a stored rotation above the limit is rejected with DERIVATION_INVALID instead of biasing the mapping
rotation_residual.why: the map uses the stored matrix, not an ideal rotation, so the residual contributes |s| * eps_R * |p - c| to the forward error and eps_R * |m - t| / |s| to the inverse error; the term is included in both bounds so any accepted matrix keeps the bound conservative

derived_transform.operation_accounting: forward: 1 subtraction, 3 products and 2 sums for R*d, 1 scale, 1 translation sum = 8 roundings; gamma order 10 adds a 2-operation safety margin; inverse uses the same accounting with the division by s
derived_transform.acceptance: measured absolute error per component must be less than or equal to the bound computed from the actual inputs
derived_transform.precision_limit_rule: derivation is rejected with PRECISION_LIMIT when bound_rt exceeds precision_limit_ratio * L_min, where L_min is the smallest distance between two distinct source control points and precision_limit_ratio is frozen below

non_coplanarity.raw_measure: V = (p2-p1) . ((p3-p1) x (p4-p1)), six times the signed tetrahedron volume for four control points
non_coplanarity.roundoff_bound: absolute uncertainty of Vhat is below 1e-14 for the supported coordinate range, leaving more than four orders of magnitude of margin to the stable threshold
non_coplanarity.stable_rule: handedness (sign of V) is only asserted when abs(Vhat) > stable_threshold
non_coplanarity.degenerate_rule: abs(Vhat) <= stable_threshold marks the path as degenerate (near planar or collinear); the input stays valid, the degenerate flag is reported and chirality is not asserted
non_coplanarity.scale_rule: Vhat is invariant under translation, proper rotation and positive uniform scaling; V scales with s^3
non_coplanarity.order_rule: V is computed on the N to C path order. Reversing the whole path is an even permutation of the four vertices, so V keeps its sign: the path direction is a separate attribute and direction sensitive quantities (tangent, signed torsion) must be defined on the ordered path. A reflection (det(R) = -1) flips the sign of V, which is how a left handed frame is detected.
non_coplanarity.reflection_rule: det(R) = -1 flips the sign of V; derivation rejects improper transforms with DERIVATION_INVALID

withdrawn.reason: the bound grows with coordinate magnitude, so at the supported maximum of 1e6 scene_unit it permits 1e-3 scene_unit of deviation, which is 1000 times the coincidence threshold and can mask a real small edit or a small Z displacement

counterexample.validity: the two points are distinct and above the 1e-6 coincidence threshold, so the variant is a legal new revision
counterexample.old_effect: 0.0001 is smaller than the withdrawn tolerance 1e-3, so the edit could be treated as a repeat
counterexample.new_effect: source coordinates compare exactly, so the semantic_digest differs and the change is detected

source_graph.identity: producer_instance_id + graph_id + revision; import_id assigned by the receiver
source_graph.note: exact accepted snapshot; never edited in place

derived_draft.edits: every edit produces a new draft_revision

facets.maximum_status: DEFERRED to G0/P3 model capability evidence

target_residue_count.note: P0 fixes the representation and refuses to invent a model limit; the precedented range stays NOT_RUN until G0/P3 evidence exists

deployment.preflight: OPTIONS with Access-Control-Allow-Origin, Access-Control-Allow-Methods GET/POST/OPTIONS, Access-Control-Allow-Headers Content-Type/Idempotency-Key, Access-Control-Max-Age 600
deployment.session: loopback bind, single local user, no cookie session
deployment.storage: SQLite, candidate; final path and transaction settings frozen in P5-I

http_500_rule.meaning: definite failure with no success receipt (persistence did not report success)
http_500_rule.manual_retry: the user may retry explicitly, and the retry must reuse the original Idempotency-Key and the byte identical snapshot; a 200 on retry means the earlier attempt had committed (converge to confirmed), a 201 means this attempt succeeded
http_500_rule.source_graph: the source graph is preserved and is not modified by a failed storage attempt

retry_policy.retry_requires: the identical original Idempotency-Key and the byte-identical original snapshot
retry_policy.retry_after: honour Retry-After when present on 429 or 503
retry_policy.unknown_outcome_state: PTG keeps the submission in 'result pending' and reconciles with the same key or with GET once the receipt or import id is known
